description:
Lessons from the World's Oldest Businesses 
A preview of his forthcoming book, anchored on Hoshi Ryokan in Japan — founded in 718 AD, now run by the 47th-generation owner.

See the full stream of the event here: https://youtube.com/live/V3V7bqLGP9o
summary: The speaker argues that the secret to Hoshi Ryokan's 1,300-year endurance is a philosophy of stewardship that prioritizes serving guests and maintaining the business's health over maximizing shareholder value. He illustrates this by describing how the founder gave away the hot spring rather than extracting profits, and how the current leader serves everyone from monks to emperors without optimizing for the highest-paying customer.
